items.stem: A training step sometimes reruns after a transient worker crash. Why should it be written to be idempotent?

options.text: Re-running it produces the same result and no duplicate side effects
options.rationale: Correct: idempotent steps can be safely retried, which is the whole point of orchestrated retries.

options.text: It makes the step run faster on the second attempt
options.rationale: Idempotency is about correctness under retries, not speed.

options.text: It guarantees the upstream data is fresh
options.rationale: Freshness is handled by sensors/scheduling, not idempotency.

options.text: It removes the need for any monitoring
options.rationale: Monitoring is still required regardless of idempotency.

items.explanation: Correct: idempotent steps can be safely retried, which is the whole point of orchestrated retries.

items.stem: A daily job depends on a partner file that arrives at an unpredictable time. Which TWO choices make the pipeline react to the data rather than the clock? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use a sensor/trigger that waits for the file to land
options.rationale: Correct: a sensor blocks until the dependency exists, making the run data-aware.

options.text: Emit an event when the file lands and start the DAG from it
options.rationale: Correct: event-driven triggering starts work exactly when data is ready.

options.text: Schedule the job 6 hours after midnight and hope the file arrived
options.rationale: A fixed offset is still clock-based and fails when the file is late.

options.text: Increase the number of retries on the first step
options.rationale: Retries do not make the job aware of data readiness.

items.explanation: Correct: a sensor blocks until the dependency exists, making the run data-aware.

items.stem: A step needs to hand a 5 GB dataset to the next step. What is the recommended pattern?

options.text: Write the data to shared object storage and pass only a reference/URI
options.rationale: Correct: pass a pointer; keep bulk data out of the orchestrator's metadata channel.

options.text: Serialize the whole dataset through the orchestrator's XCom/metadata channel
options.rationale: Metadata channels are for small values and will choke or fail on large data.

options.text: Recompute the dataset in the next step from scratch
options.rationale: Wasteful and breaks lineage; the data already exists.

options.text: Email the dataset to the next task

items.explanation: Correct: pass a pointer; keep bulk data out of the orchestrator's metadata channel.
